title: Paris at Christmas: markets, lights and what's open in 2026
author: Brogan
intro: Paris at Christmas means lights on the Champs-Élysées, Christmas markets in the Tuileries, a giant tree under the Galeries Lafayette dome and skating at the Grand Palais. Here are the 2026 dates, what to expect and how to plan a short trip from the UK.
seo_title: Paris at Christmas 2026: markets, lights and dates
seo_description: Champs-Élysées lights expected from 22 November 2026, Tuileries market from mid-November, Grand Palais rink 13 Dec to 6 Jan. Dates, tips and trains.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Lights on:** expected 22 November
- **Markets:** mid-Nov to early Jan
- **Grand Palais rink:** 13 Dec to 6 Jan
- **From London:** about 2¼ hrs by Eurostar

These are the dates published so far for Christmas 2026. Some were still to be confirmed when we checked in early November, so check each one's official website before you book around it. December in Paris is cold, at about 8°C by day, so pack a warm coat.

sections.text:

The big department store windows and trees usually appear in mid-November and stay up until early January.

sections.heading: The lights and the department stores
sections.text:
The Champs-Élysées lights are the start of Christmas in Paris. The avenue's trees are wrapped in lights from the Arc de Triomphe down to Place de la Concorde, and they usually stay on every evening until early January.

On Boulevard Haussmann, the **Galeries Lafayette** hangs a giant Christmas tree under its glass dome, and both it and **Printemps** next door fill their street windows with animated displays. The free rooftop terrace at Galeries Lafayette has one of the best views over the city.

Tip: the department stores are busiest on December weekends. Go on a weekday morning to see the tree and the windows without the crowds.

sections.heading: The Christmas markets
sections.text:
Paris's markets are smaller and more fairground-like than the famous ones in Germany or Alsace, but they're fun for an evening:

- **Tuileries Garden:** the biggest, with food stalls, mulled wine and a big wheel, between the Louvre and Place de la Concorde.
- **Champs-Élysées:** returning this year, reportedly after nearly a decade away.
- **La Défense:** one of the largest in the Paris region, in the business district just west of the city.
- **Notre-Dame:** a small market across the river from the cathedral, which reopened in December 2024.

If markets are the main reason for your trip, [Strasbourg](/destinations/strasbourg) has France's most famous one, and our [Strasbourg or Colmar at Christmas](/blog/strasbourg-or-colmar-at-christmas) post compares the two. Our guide to [Christmas markets by train from London](/blog/christmas-markets-by-train-from-london) covers more.

sections.heading: Skating, Disneyland and Christmas Day
sections.text:
The **Grand Palais** turns its glass-roofed hall into a giant indoor ice rink from 13 December 2026 to 6 January 2027, and tickets usually need booking. [Disneyland Paris](/destinations/disneyland-paris) also has its Christmas season, with a parade and decorations, about 40 minutes from the city by RER.

On Christmas Day itself, many museums and shops close, including the Louvre. Restaurants that open usually offer set menus, which need booking well ahead.

Watch out: some sights also close or shorten their hours on 1 January, and the days before Christmas and New Year are among the busiest of the season. Check opening times for the dates you're there.

sections.heading: Getting there and how long to stay
sections.text:
Eurostar takes about 2¼ hours from London St Pancras to Paris Gare du Nord, arriving in the city centre, which makes Paris one of the easiest Christmas breaks from the UK. You can also fly from most UK airports in about an hour and a quarter. Paris is an hour ahead.

- **Two nights** is enough for the lights, a market and the department stores.
- **Three or four nights** lets you add a day at Disneyland or a trip out to Versailles.

Our [Paris guide](/destinations/paris) has more on the city through the year, and [where you can go on the Eurostar](/blog/where-can-you-go-on-the-eurostar) has ideas for combining it with [Brussels](/destinations/brussels) or [Bruges](/destinations/bruges). Torn between Paris and another Christmas city? Add them to somewhere.party and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: When do the Paris Christmas lights go on in 2026?
faqs.answer: The Champs-Élysées lights are expected to be switched on on Sunday 22 November 2026, and usually stay on until early January.

faqs.question: When is the Paris Christmas market in the Tuileries?
faqs.answer: It usually runs from mid-November to early January. Check the official dates before you travel, as they're confirmed close to opening.

faqs.question: Is Paris worth visiting at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the lights, the department store windows, the markets and skating at the Grand Palais. It's cold, at about 8°C by day, and busy at weekends.

faqs.question: Is the Louvre open on Christmas Day?
faqs.answer: No. The Louvre is closed on 25 December and 1 January, and many other museums close on Christmas Day too.
